sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the essential joy of the Giving of the Torah, which was like a wedding, is drawn down through service and is present in every mitzvah, as each Jew is God's only son, making the joy of each mitzvah like the joy of a wedding that breaks all boundaries.

translations.translation: And just as it was on the day of His wedding, this is the Giving of the Torah,
that then there was the drawing down of the essential joy, etc.,
(as explained in the maamar,
that the main joy that breaks all boundaries is the joy of marriage),
and the drawing down then was through service,
for on the day of His wedding, this is the Giving of the Torah, it refers to the second Tablets,
and the concept of the second Tablets is that they were given specifically through service.
And likewise is it in the fulfillment of every mitzvah,
that through every mitzvah one must say "For the sake of the union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah," as it is brought in Pri Etz Chaim,
and that which we say "For the sake of the union" only once before prayer is because this saying is an ongoing action for the entire day.
And since each and every Jew is the only son of the Holy One, blessed be He, according to the well-known teaching of the Baal Shem Tov,
and it is written,
"My firstborn son, Israel," in the singular,
and also at the Giving of the Torah it was said to each and every Jew, "I am
the L-rd your G-d," in the singular,
therefore,
the joy above that is in the fulfillment of every mitzvah of each and every Jew is the joy of the Holy One, blessed be He, at the wedding of His only son,
for this joy breaks all boundaries.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that in the month of Elul, especially on Shabbos, the joy of the union between God and the Jewish people is even greater, and every addition in Torah and mitzvos breaks all boundaries, including those of exile, hastening the future redemption.

translations.translation: And particularly in the month of Elul,
when the King is in the field with each and every Jew,
and receives each and every one with a pleasant countenance and shows them a smiling face,
and Elul is an acronym for "I am to my Beloved and my Beloved is to me,"
for even "beloved" refers to Zeir Anpin and Nukvah, whose union is only intermittent,
nevertheless, in the month of Elul they are united in one word.
And from this it is understood,
that in addition to the concept of the joy of marriage
(the union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah)
that exists throughout the year by virtue of the fulfillment of the mitzvos,
in the month of Elul it is with even greater intensity.
And particularly on the Shabbosos of the month of Elul.
For in the month of Elul we blow the shofar in order to warn Israel to repent, as it is written,
"If a shofar is blown in a city, will the people not tremble?"
Thus, in Elul there is also the concept of fear and trembling.
However, this is only on weekdays,
but not so on the Shabbosos of the month of Elul,
for the concept of fear and trembling of Elul, ostensibly,
(in a revealed way)
are not present on Shabbos,
for on Shabbos we do not blow the shofar, and on Shabbos there is no sadness,
and the main activity of Elul on the Shabbos days is the concept of "I am to my Beloved and my Beloved is to me,"
the joy of the marriage of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Congregation of Israel.
And from this it is understood,
that every addition in Torah and mitzvos,
and particularly in the month of Elul,
breaks all boundaries,
including also the boundaries of exile,
for every addition in Torah and mitzvos
(whose concept is the opposite of exile)
hastens the future redemption,
"On that day shall there be, etc.,"
"Beis Pei Yud Hei,"
meaning that also Vav-Hei will be like Yud-Hei,
and just as Yud-Hei, their union is constant,
so too, the aspect of Vav-Hei, their union will be constant,
in the future redemption,
for then there will be the concept of marriage,
as it is brought in Shemos Rabbah,
that now it is the concept of betrothal, and in the future there will be the marriage,
speedily in our days, literally.
